question: What are the candidate therapeutic targets, immune pathways and biomarkers in ulcerative colitis with the strongest convergent evidence?

findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence gene and is up in UC in all eight cohorts. In the same patients inflamed mucosa exceeds non-inflamed mucosa (paired log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]), with only a small rise in non-inflamed versus control [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]. The change holds after adjustment for segment, age and sex. Caveat for immune genes: a bulk increase can come from infiltrating neutrophils rather than a change inside the tissue, which the cell-context specialist should confirm.

CXCL8 (IL-8) is strongly and reproducibly raised in all eight cohorts, with a pooled log2FC given here [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687]. As an immune-cell-rich chemokine, part of the bulk signal may come from infiltrating cells.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in all eight cohorts and local to inflamed mucosa: paired inflamed versus non-inflamed log2FC [gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.0008], whereas non-inflamed versus control is barely changed [gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.1971]. This looks like an inflammation-driven response; immune-cell contribution to the bulk signal is possible.

IDO1 is up in all eight cohorts and the change replicates as protein in an independent proteomics study [gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917].

CHI3L1 has one of the largest pooled increases [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913], significant in all eight cohorts and robust to segment, age and sex adjustment. At protein level the direction agrees but the effect is much smaller [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607] and the authors did not call it significant, so the RNA magnitude overstates the protein change.

HMGCS2 is lost in all eight cohorts and the loss is specific to inflamed mucosa: non-inflamed versus control is flat [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649], while the paired inflamed versus non-inflamed contrast is strongly negative. Protein falls too [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094] and the change holds after adjustment, making it a local-inflammation biomarker rather than a target.

AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.7633], significantly down in all eight cohorts, making it a biomarker candidate rather than a target.

MMP3 is strongly induced [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.822] in all eight cohorts and is also higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa of the same patient, in line with a tissue-remodelling programme.
DUOX2 rises in all eight cohorts [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.3033] and is higher in inflamed mucosa within patients, a local inflammation biomarker.

JAK2 has strong genetic and drug support but only a modest expression change [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.833], though significantly up in all eight cohorts. Its rank comes from genetics and tractability rather than expression magnitude.
S100A8 is up in all eight cohorts. As an immune-cell-rich gene, its bulk increase may partly reflect infiltrating cells, which the cell-context specialist should check.
TREM1 is up in all eight cohorts and higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa; a phase 2 inhibitor (nangibotide) is listed. Its bulk rise may reflect infiltrating myeloid cells.

caveats: Pooled log2FC are on mixed RNA-seq and microarray scales; compare direction and significance across cohorts, not sizes. Heterogeneity (I2) is high for nearly all top genes.
Bulk RNA of inflamed mucosa includes infiltrating neutrophils and myeloid cells; CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8, TREM1 and CD274 may reflect composition. The cell-context specialist must check.
Protein support is partial: only some genes are measured in the proteomics study, and the CHI3L1 protein effect was far smaller than the RNA effect.
Convergence ranking is driven by genetics and tractability for CXCR2, JAK2 and CD274.
Only CXCR2, CHI3L1 and HMGCS2 were tested with adjusted_change; only CHI3L1, IDO1 and HMGCS2 with protein_level.

findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top-ranked convergence gene, but the curated corpus holds no verbatim-validated relation for it, a limit of the corpus: Europe PMC returns many mouse colitis papers on CXCR2. The literature support is indirect: a Mendelian randomization, colocalization and transcriptomic study proposes CXCR1 and CXCR2 as neutrophil extracellular trap-related treatment targets in UC, and a separate eQTL/pQTL/transcriptome study ties the CXCL5/CXCR2 axis to neutrophil chemotaxis in UC.

CXCR1 has no verbatim-validated literature relation in the corpus. It shares the genetic-colocalization paper that nominates CXCR1 and CXCR2 as neutrophil extracellular trap-related UC targets, so the evidence is a single bioinformatic or genetic study.

The literature says the CXCL8 axis with its receptors participates in UC pathogenesis through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signalling. In a blood RNA-seq validation set CXCL8 was among the best diagnostic genes for IBD, second to ITGA5. This is IBD rather than UC-specific, and it is bioinformatic.

IDO1 has the most mechanistic and interventional support among the targets. IDO1 expression was elevated in UC patients and correlated with M1 macrophage polarization in both human data and colitis mice. IDO1 drove M1 polarization via the ER stress GRP78-XBP1 pathway. An IDO1 inhibitor ameliorated DSS colitis in mice. All of this comes from one study, with no UC clinical trial.

MMP1 was reported as a diagnostic marker of UC-associated CRC with high AUC, and ilomastat was predicted in silico as an inhibitor. MMP1 transcripts modified by mirikizumab correlate with Mayo score, Geboes score and Robarts Histopathology Index, which supports MMP1 as a pharmacodynamic marker of disease activity. A hub-gene analysis also links MMP1 to macrophage infiltration.

CHI3L1 was significantly upregulated in UC patients and correlated with the NLRP3 inflammasome. It promoted macrophage pyroptosis via a BCAT1/NF-kappaB axis, and inhibiting CHI3L1 was protective. Velpatasvir binding to recombinant CHI3L1 was shown by microscale thermophoresis. This rests on a few preclinical or bioinformatic studies, and no approved drug exists.

DUOX2 protein was among the most elevated in inflamed UC biopsies versus healthy controls, together with HLA-DRA, CD74 and LCN2. Herbal formula TLXDS reduced UC by inhibiting DUOX2 overexpression, and DUOX2 was proposed as a ferroptosis-linked and diagnostic candidate. The evidence is preclinical, and DUOX2 has no drug.

CXCL1 is repeatedly nominated as a diagnostic or activity marker across independent bioinformatic studies, but its standalone accuracy was modest in one of them. It appeared within a five-gene combined diagnostic model with very high accuracy, whereas CXCL1 alone was only a fair activity marker.

S100A9 expression showed excellent performance for diagnosing active UC and was upregulated in UC. IRF5 represses S100A9 and limits G-MDSC accumulation. In treatment responders S100A9 was downregulated in resident macrophages, which suggests a response signal from myeloid cells rather than the epithelium.

LCN2 was upregulated in UC and IBD. In a study of UC-associated carcinogenesis its expression was higher in short-duration UC than in long-duration UC, higher in long-duration UC than in UC-associated cancer, and higher in all of them than in normal tissue. This gives a possible disease-duration confounder for its use as a marker.
HMGCS2 is consistently reported as decreased in UC with high diagnostic value in two studies. This is a downregulated epithelial metabolic marker and not a drug target.
SLC26A3 was significantly lower in UC patients in ONT-RNA-seq. That is the only verbatim-validated literature relation for it in the corpus.

caveats: Verbatim-validated relations are absent for CXCR2, CXCR1, CD274, JAK2, INHBA, IL2RA and FCGR2A, which are the genetically supported targets. Their support is genetic or Open Targets, not literature. Literature for CXCR1/2 comes only from search chunks.
Many biomarker claims come from bioinformatic hub-gene or machine-learning studies that mostly lack external clinical validation.
A tofacitinib study in the corpus reports differential effects on macrophage activation contributing to non-response. JAK2 itself has no validated relation here.
IDO1 and CHI3L1 mechanism evidence is from single preclinical studies with no UC trial.
No numeric values are cited in the findings.

findings.statement: CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking, with meta-analysis up-regulation in biopsies [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.84] and a high Open Targets genetic association score. Several CXCR2 antagonists reached clinical trials (reparixin phase 3, outside UC); in UC, SB-656933 and navarixin (SCH-527123) went no further than phase 2, the highest UC stage in the clinical-indications record.

CXCR2 has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so MR is not tested (absence of evidence, not evidence against). Mouse literature tests CXCR2 in colitis in many papers, including a selective antagonist that ameliorated acute colitis, but MGI has no curated single-gene colitis phenotype. Safety: not strongly constrained, no curated safety events and no pleiotropic traits sharing the signal, but navarixin, as MK-7123, caused a dose-dependent decrease in absolute neutrophil count in a COPD trial.

Plasma PD-L1 (CD274) is protective in MR: higher protein lowers UC risk, an odds ratio per SD of [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595], with colocalisation with an IBD GWAS signal and replication in FinnGen. CD274 is also up-regulated in biopsies, the opposite direction, so PD-L1-blocking antibodies such as atezolizumab (recorded at Phase 4) would act against the genetic direction.

CD274 MR sensitivity: significant heterogeneity across the three instruments, no directional pleiotropy by the Egger intercept, Steiger direction correct. Mouse colitis literature is sparse and MGI has no phenotype. Not strongly constrained, no known safety events.

IL12B is the top Open Targets UC target and a strong plasma MR hit: higher protein raises UC risk, odds ratio per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]. It colocalises with an IBD GWAS signal and replicates in FinnGen, so inhibition is the protective direction. No gut eQTL instrument.

CXCL8 is strongly and consistently up-regulated in biopsies and has anti-IL-8 antibodies recorded in Phase 2 (ABX-IL8, adakitug), but its Open Targets genetic association score is zero, and plasma MR is null (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]) with no replication in FinnGen. Its signal likely reflects neutrophil-driven inflammation rather than causal genetics.

CXCL5 is up-regulated in biopsies, yet plasma MR suggests higher protein is protective, odds ratio per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]. It replicates in FinnGen but does not colocalise with IBD GWAS and uses a tag variant, so a neighbouring causal variant cannot be excluded. This conflicts with a pro-inflammatory chemokine interpretation.

SLC26A3 is down-regulated in inflamed mucosa and has a moderate Open Targets genetic association. In IBDverse gut cell-type eQTL (OLFM4+ crypt enterocyte progenitors) higher expression raises UC risk, odds ratio per SD [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607], with colocalisation and replication in FinnGen. Direction is opposite to the biopsy decrease, so loss in disease may be a response; there is no drug and no plasma pQTL.

JAK2 has a high Open Targets association (second among known UC targets in the disease target list) and approved or clinical inhibitors, but only a small biopsy change. No pQTL or eQTL instrument, so MR is not tested.

CHI3L1 is one of the strongest, fully replicated up-regulated genes (all cohorts same direction) but its Open Targets genetic association score is zero and no drug is recorded, so it is a biomarker candidate rather than a genetically supported target.

AQP9 is strongly up-regulated and replicated, also higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa, but its Open Targets genetic association score is zero and no drug is recorded, so it is an expression-led biomarker candidate.

MMP7 is up-regulated and replicated and has MMP inhibitors or doxycycline recorded in other indications (marimastat Phase 3), but has no genetic association with UC, so support is expression and literature only.

caveats: Plasma MR (UKB-PPP) reflects blood protein, not mucosal protein; many top-ranked genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, JAK2, SLC26A3 plasma) have no cis-pQTL and are not tested, which is not evidence against them.
The top-ranked expression genes mostly lack genetic support; neutrophil and chemokine signals may come from infiltrating immune cells.
Drugs listed are as returned by Open Targets in any indication, not UC trials; MGI had no curated colitis phenotype for CXCR2 or CD274.
Not queried within budget: CXCR1, IDO1, MMP1, IL1B, IL6, FCGR2A, JAK1/3, TYK2, STRING interactions.

findings.statement: CXCR2 transcripts in inflamed mucosa are almost entirely neutrophil. Smillie 2019 labels it T/NK from cells that barely express it (at most two percent of the cells of its leading clusters), and this does not replicate: Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026 give myeloid, and only GSE282122 agrees with T/NK. The neutrophil share in Gubatan 2026 is [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]. After composition adjustment the change is partly_composition, and the adjusted log2FC is [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]. The top convergence rank is therefore mainly a marker of neutrophil influx. A neutrophil-directed CXCR1 and CXCR2 antagonist is still plausible, but it acts on arriving cells, not on a change inside the tissue.

CXCR1 behaves like CXCR2: nearly all its transcripts in inflamed UC mucosa come from neutrophils (Gubatan 2026). The composition model leaves the change partly_composition, with a small fraction of the unadjusted effect retained, [gene=CXCR1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.195]. The adjusted change stays significant, but most of the bulk signal reflects neutrophil arrival. Adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated.

CXCL8 attribution to myeloid cells replicates in all three other atlases (Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026, GSE282122), with macrophages leading in Smillie 2019. Neutrophils also make most of its transcripts in Gubatan 2026, with neutrophil share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]. The composition verdict is composition and the adjusted change loses significance, with adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0525]. The bulk rise mostly tracks myeloid and neutrophil influx, so CXCL8 is a marker of cell arrival. It is not proof of a tissue-intrinsic change, because the adjustment can over-correct.

IDO1 is myeloid in Smillie 2019 (macrophages and DC1), and the attribution replicates in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122. Gubatan 2026 instead gives epithelial, mainly enterocytes, so the producing lineage is not unique. Neutrophils contribute little. The bulk increase is partly_composition but stays significant after adjustment, with adjusted log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]. This points to a change inside the tissue in myeloid cells and enterocytes, which would suit a cell-type target.

MMP1 is made by stromal cells, mainly inflammatory fibroblasts, with the dominant lineage share in Smillie 2019 at [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]. The attribution replicates in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122. Visium deconvolution gives inflammatory fibroblasts the largest in situ contribution, [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.568]. The bulk change keeps significance after composition adjustment, with adjusted log2FC [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]. This is evidence of a tissue change inside fibroblasts. CosMx detection is at background, so single-cell spatial data do not confirm it.

DUOX2 is epithelial (enterocytes), with the dominant lineage share in Smillie 2019 at [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]. The attribution replicates in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122, and Xenium and Visium both place it in epithelium. Neutrophils contribute little. The adjusted change stays significant, with adjusted log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]. This is a strong tissue-intrinsic epithelial change, not neutrophil influx.

CHI3L1 is stromal (inflammatory fibroblasts) in Smillie 2019, replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, while Gubatan 2026 gives myeloid. Neutrophils also contribute in Gubatan 2026, with neutrophil share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.466]. The change is partly_composition and stays significant after adjustment, with adjusted log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]. It is both a fibroblast activation marker and a partial neutrophil-influx marker.

TREM1 is myeloid (macrophages and inflammatory monocytes), replicated in all three other atlases, and neutrophils make most of its transcripts in Gubatan 2026, with neutrophil share [gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894]. The change is partly_composition and stays significant after adjustment, with adjusted log2FC [gene=TREM1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.6621]. TREM1 is both a myeloid and neutrophil influx marker and a possible change in activation within those cells.

CD274 (PD-L1) has a diffuse source across plasma cells, macrophages, enterocytes and neutrophils, so no single lineage dominates. Replication is formally met (Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026 agree with myeloid, GSE282122 gives T/NK). Neutrophils make a large share in Gubatan 2026, with neutrophil share [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]. The change is partly_composition and stays significant after adjustment, with adjusted log2FC [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]. It fits an inflammation-induced checkpoint response, not a single-cell-type target.

AQP9 is a neutrophil-dominated transcript in inflamed mucosa (Gubatan 2026), so its high convergence score largely reflects neutrophil influx. The change is partly_composition but remains significant after adjustment, with adjusted log2FC [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8551]. It is best used as an influx marker, with some residual tissue change.

S100A8 comes mostly from neutrophils in Gubatan 2026, so it is a marker of neutrophil influx. The bulk change is partly_composition and stays significant after adjustment, with adjusted log2FC [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231]. Part of this may be real activation of resident cells, but the neutrophil share is large.

SLC26A2 is down in UC bulk, and the loss is intrinsic to the tissue and not driven by neutrophils, with neutrophil share [gene=SLC26A2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.014]. The decrease stays significant after composition adjustment, with verdict intrinsic and adjusted log2FC [gene=SLC26A2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-1.4638]. This is strong evidence of an epithelial program lost within the inflamed tissue. It points to a mechanism and a restoration biomarker, not a candidate for inhibition.

caveats: Smillie 2019 captured no neutrophils, so its lineage call is wrong for neutrophil genes (CXCR2); Gubatan 2026 is the only atlas with neutrophil states.

Composition adjustment can over-correct, because lineage scores also rise when resident cells activate. A gene that loses significance (CXCL8) is not proof of pure influx, and a gene that keeps it is strong evidence of a tissue change.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance. Dissociation protocols enrich some fractions.
MMP1 is at background on CosMx and not on the Xenium panel, so spatial support rests on Visium spot deconvolution.
Only the leading candidates were profiled; other genes in the top 40 (for example the MMPs, REG family, CLDN2, HMGCS2) were not checked for cell attribution here.

findings.statement: CXCL8 is up in all eight cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687]) and ranks third in convergence. It is the ligand of the neutrophil circuit, neutrophil CXCL8 to CXCR2 and ACKR1 (see the CXCR2 and ACKR1 findings). This is co-expression, not proof of signalling.

In the Gubatan single-cell data, the CXCL8 to ACKR1 link from neutrophil states (generic Neutrophil, CXCR4, OSM, MX1, PADI4) to ACKR1 endothelium has some of the highest scores seen, and the generic Neutrophil sender rose in inflamed versus uninflamed mucosa. This is co-expression only, and ACKR1 is an atypical chemokine receptor that presents chemokines and does not signal conventionally.

Cell source of CXCL8 depends on the atlas. Without neutrophils (Smillie), macrophages and other myeloid cells make most CXCL8 and the myeloid lineage replicates in all three other atlases. When neutrophils are included (Gubatan), neutrophils make most of the CXCL8 transcripts, so the signal in bulk biopsies is largely infiltrating immune cells and not a change of the epithelium or stroma.

CXCR2 is rank 1 in the convergence ranking, with up-regulation in all eight cohorts for CXCR2 and Open Targets genetic support. Its antagonists reached clinical trials: reparixin (phase 3) and ladarixin and SX-682 (phase 2) outside UC, and in UC navarixin and SB-656933, which went no further than phase 2. Its transcripts sit in neutrophils in the single-cell data, and CXCR2 is not replicated as a stromal or T/NK gene across atlases, so it is a neutrophil-recruitment target and not a tissue-intrinsic one.

CXCR2 receivers are neutrophil states. The CXCL8 to CXCR2 link from Neutrophil CXCR4 to the generic Neutrophil state rose strongly in inflamed versus uninflamed mucosa, consistent with a feed-forward neutrophil recruitment loop. This is co-expression only.

Inflammatory fibroblasts are a stromal sender of CXCL1 to CXCR2 on neutrophils, and the link to the generic Neutrophil state rose strongly in inflamed mucosa. Absolute scores are far lower than the neutrophil CXCL8 circuit. No CXCL1 or CXCL5 drug is listed.

The expected neutrophil OSM to inflammatory fibroblast circuit is weak in this dataset. OSM to IL6ST from Neutrophil OSM to LP fibroblast has a low score and fell versus uninflamed mucosa. Only the Neutrophil PADI4 sender is new in inflamed tissue, with a small score. No inflammatory-fibroblast receiver appeared among the top pairs, so this circuit is not supported here.

IL1B is up in all eight cohorts and has drugs in Open Targets (canakinumab approved, for other diseases). In single-cell data its strongest links go to IL1R2, a decoy receptor, on neutrophil states, sent by monocyte-derived macrophages and neutrophils. So high co-expression does not by itself imply productive IL-1 signalling.

NFkB and TNFa pathway activity are up in all eight cohorts, with the strongest t in the NFkB pathway reaching [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=18.79] in GSE206285. Such broad pathways are poor at discriminating specific circuits.

JAK-STAT, TGFb, EGFR, MAPK, PI3K and Hypoxia pathways are up in all eight cohorts, and WNT in seven of eight (not in GSE73661). Inflamed mucosa activates many pathways at once, so concordance alone is not specific.

STAT3 regulon activity is up in all eight cohorts (t in GSE193677 [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6]), and AP1 is also up in all eight cohorts. TF activity is inferred from target genes, not from the TF mRNA.

Not all pathways replicate. VEGF is up in only four cohorts, and Androgen is down in four and up in one, so neither is a consistent signature. These weaker pathways should not be prioritized over the pathways that rise in every cohort.

TREM1 is up in all eight cohorts and has a phase 2 drug (nangibotide), but it returned no ligand-receptor pair above expression thresholds in the single-cell data, so no sender or receiver circuit can be named for it.
AQP9 is up in all eight cohorts, but it has no drug and no genetic support in this ranking, so it is an undrugged, biomarker-like candidate and not a validated target.

caveats: Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression (ligand times receptor mean CP10K) in one single-cell dataset, not signalling.
Pathway and TF activities are inferred by decoupler from bulk mucosal transcriptomes, so they largely reflect immune infiltration and cannot separate tissue-intrinsic change from cell composition.
Many top-ranked genes (CXCL8, CXCL1, S100A8/9, MMPs, AQP9) are neutrophil or myeloid markers, so their ranking may track neutrophil abundance in inflamed biopsies.
IL-23 and integrin axes were not queried in detail; anti-TNF, JAK inhibitor and integrin drug status is not supported by cited records here.
Only top communication rows per gene were read.

findings.statement: CXCR2 leads the convergence ranking, with expression, replication across cohorts, genetics, literature and tractability (several CXCR1 and CXCR2 antagonists in clinical development) all contributing.

Higher baseline CXCR2 is associated with ustekinumab non-response, but it also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders, so it marks severity rather than a ustekinumab-specific mechanism. Ustekinumab BH padj was [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6] and placebo BH padj was [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126].

CXCL8 is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders, but the placebo arm shows the same direction, so this is a severity signal. Ustekinumab BH padj was [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102] and UNIFI placebo BH padj was [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154]. Golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab arms did not survive correction.

In the adalimumab single-cell atlas (GSE282122, a small cohort of remitters and non-remitters), CXCL8 showed no baseline difference between remitters and non-remitters in any cell state. It changed after treatment in some states, for example a decrease in cycling mononuclear phagocytes with BH padj [gene=CXCL8; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.1.padj=0.0253].

OSM is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]). The UNIFI placebo arm is not significant (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), but the drug-versus-placebo interaction is not significant either (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.974]), so drug specificity is not shown. The golimumab arm did not survive correction.

TREM1 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) but also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders (BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), consistent with a general severity marker. Other biologic arms did not survive correction.

IL11 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]), but UNIFI placebo non-responders also differ (BH padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]), so it again points to severity.

Negative result: baseline IL23A is not associated with ustekinumab response (BH padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]), so expression of an IL-23 subunit does not stratify response to ustekinumab, which blocks IL-23 through its IL12B (p40) subunit.
Negative result: baseline ITGB7 is flat for vedolizumab response (BH padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]).

The PROGENy TNFa pathway is higher in non-responders to ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and also in infliximab, vedolizumab, golimumab and UNIFI placebo arms, so it is a general severity axis. It is not significant in PURSUIT placebo (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]) or in the PROTECT mesalazine arm (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.5-ASA (PROTECT).padj=0.414]).

The TGFb pathway is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]), so it is not drug-specific.

JAK-STAT pathway activity is higher in non-responders for ustekinumab, infliximab and PROTECT corticosteroids, but not for golimumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.204]), so the signal does not hold across all anti-TNF cohorts.

CHRDL2 is a first-in-class opportunity that is up in cohorts [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=7]. Its transcripts are stromal, mostly inflammatory fibroblasts, with the stromal lineage agreeing in other atlases [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; other_atlases_agreeing=3] (Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026, GSE282122). The composition verdict is partly composition and an antibody is the predicted modality. Missing: any response-association data or functional validation.

CPXM1 is stromal in Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, but Gubatan 2026 assigns it to the epithelial lineage. The discovery screen labels it partly composition and an antibody-tractable first-in-class opportunity, so part of its increase may reflect fibroblast expansion. Missing: genetics and response data.

LAX1 passes the screen but its lineage does not replicate. Smillie 2019 and GSE282122 call it T/NK, while Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026 call it plasma. It is largely immune-cell derived and partly composition, so it is more a marker of infiltrating lymphocytes and plasma cells than a tissue change.

XKR9 is classed as intrinsic by the composition filter, with an epithelial lineage replicated in Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122 (not Garrido-Trigo 2023, which calls it plasma). Evidence is thin, with elevation in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts and low expression in each epithelial cluster. Missing: response data and functional evidence.

GLT1D1 is classed as composition-driven and its transcripts are mostly neutrophil-derived, so it reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than an intrinsic tissue change. It should be treated as a weak target despite its first-in-class label.

caveats: Response cohorts are small outside UNIFI (golimumab, infliximab, vedolizumab, etrolizumab, ACT1), so null results there are underpowered rather than evidence of absence.
Drug-versus-placebo interactions were not significant for the genes checked, so ustekinumab-specific mechanisms are not demonstrated.
The anti-TNF single-cell atlas has few patients: leads only.
Discovery candidates are mostly partly composition-driven; 'first-in-class' reflects filters, not validated dependency.

Not run: treatment_response for TNF, CXCR1 and other ranked genes, antitnf_singlecell for most genes, or celltype_expression for the CXCR1/2 axis. Convergence-ranking numbers are not quoted since no verified field path was available.

summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in UC mucosa is a neutrophil-recruitment axis. CXCR2, CXCR1 and CXCL8 take the first three places of the convergence ranking, CXCR2 and CXCL8 are up in all eight cohorts, but single-cell data place almost all CXCR2 transcripts in neutrophils [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965] and most CXCL8 transcripts too [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873], so their bulk rise mainly reports neutrophil arrival rather than a change of the tissue itself.

Human genetics separates causes from consequences. IL12B carries a strong Open Targets genetic association with UC [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8864] and is the strongest plasma Mendelian randomisation result among this atlas's genes: genetically higher protein raises UC risk [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539], so inhibition is the protective direction. IL12B is the p40 subunit of interleukin-12 and interleukin-23: ustekinumab binds it and was more effective than placebo in UC, and the anti-p19 antibodies mirikizumab, risankizumab and guselkumab, which bind IL23A and block interleukin-23 only, were effective too, which shows that blocking interleukin-23 alone is enough; whether blocking interleukin-12 adds benefit is not settled by these trials. For CD274 (PD-L1) genetics points the other way: higher plasma protein lowers UC risk [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595].

Inside the tissue, DUOX2 in enterocytes and MMP1 in inflammatory fibroblasts keep a clear increase after the composition adjustment ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161] and [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]) and their cell source replicates across the single-cell atlases, while the epithelial gene AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss of the meta-analysis [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.7633] and HMGCS2 is among the largest losses.

Baseline CXCR2, CXCL8, TREM1 and IL11 are higher in ustekinumab non-responders, but each also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders, so they mark disease severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism. Baseline expression of the drug's own target does not predict response either: IL12B, the subunit ustekinumab binds ([gene=IL12B; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.84]), and its IL-23 partner IL23A ([gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]).

expression.text: The largest and most consistent increases in UC mucosa are remodelling, antimicrobial and neutrophil genes. CHI3L1 [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913] and MMP3 [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.822] are among the largest pooled increases of all genes up in the eight-cohort meta-analysis, and DUOX2 [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.3033] and CXCL8 [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687] are also up in all eight cohorts.

Epithelial metabolism is lost. AQP8 has the largest pooled loss of all genes down in the meta-analysis [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.7633] and falls in all eight cohorts, and HMGCS2 is among the largest losses. The loss of the epithelial transporter SLC26A2 stays significant after composition adjustment [gene=SLC26A2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-1.4638], a change of the tissue itself.

JAK2 is up in all eight cohorts but only modestly [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.833]; it has the second highest Open Targets association with UC among the genes in this atlas's graph, so its place among the candidates comes from genetics and drug history rather than expression.

inflammation.text: Most leading changes are local to inflamed mucosa. Comparing inflamed with non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients (GSE193677), CXCR2 rises [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972] with only a small change in non-inflamed versus control mucosa [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]; CD274 behaves the same way ([gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.0008] against [gene=CD274; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.1971]), and HMGCS2 is unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649], so its loss belongs to inflammation.
MMP3, DUOX2, TREM1 and AQP9 are also higher in inflamed than in non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients.

replication.text: The leading changes reproduce across cohorts: CXCR2, CHI3L1, DUOX2, JAK2 and AQP8 are significant in the same direction in all eight cohorts. At protein level, in an independent proteomics study, IDO1 [gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917] and HMGCS2 [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094] change in the same direction as RNA, whereas CHI3L1 rises much less as protein [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607] and was not called significant by the authors.

literature.text: The curated corpus holds no verbatim-checked CXCR2 relation, a limit of the corpus rather than of the field: Europe PMC returns [gene=CXCR2; type=mouse_colitis_literature; source=DATASET:EUROPEPMC_MOUSE; mouse_colitis_papers=19] mouse colitis papers on CXCR2. Among the corpus abstracts, a Mendelian randomisation, colocalisation and transcriptomic study proposes CXCR1 and CXCR2 as neutrophil extracellular trap-related treatment targets in UC, although in its Mendelian randomisation higher CXCR1 and CXCR2 expression went with lower UC risk (this atlas has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument to check it), and another ties the CXCL5 to CXCR2 axis to neutrophil chemotaxis. The cited IDO1 support is one experimental study: IDO1 was elevated in UC patients and colitis mice, drove pro-inflammatory macrophage polarisation through the GRP78-XBP1 pathway, and an IDO1 inhibitor ameliorated DSS colitis.

For biomarkers the literature is more useful. MMP1 is among the transcripts modified by mirikizumab that correlate with the modified Mayo score, Geboes score and Robarts Histopathology Index; CHI3L1 is upregulated in UC and promotes macrophage pyroptosis through BCAT1 and NF-kappaB; DUOX2 protein is among the most elevated in inflamed UC biopsies; and HMGCS2 is reported decreased in UC.

The CXCL8 axis with its receptors is described as taking part in UC pathogenesis through PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signalling, and in a blood RNA-seq validation set CXCL8 was among the best diagnostic genes for IBD, second to ITGA5, an IBD-level rather than UC-specific result. CXCL1 is nominated as a diagnostic or activity marker in several bioinformatic studies; alone it is only a fair activity marker, and its high accuracy comes within a combined multi-gene model.

external.text: Approved-target genetics behaves as a positive control. IL12B carries a strong Open Targets genetic association with UC [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8864] and is the strongest plasma Mendelian randomisation result among this atlas's genes: genetically higher protein raises UC risk [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539], the signal colocalises with an IBD GWAS locus and replicates in FinnGen, so inhibition is the protective direction.

Among expression-led candidates, genetics often points the other way. For CD274 higher plasma protein lowers UC risk [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595] although it rises in inflamed mucosa, which suggests a compensatory rise. CXCL5 is also protective in plasma [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634] but rests on a tag variant without colocalisation. SLC26A3 falls in inflamed mucosa, yet higher expression in IBDverse crypt progenitors raises UC risk [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]. CXCL8 is null in plasma (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]) and has no Open Targets genetic association.

CXCR2 has a high Open Targets genetic association score but no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so Mendelian randomisation could not test it. Two antagonists were tested in UC, SB-656933 and navarixin (SCH-527123, also coded MK-7123), and neither went beyond phase 2, the highest UC stage recorded; reparixin reached phase 3 outside UC (type I diabetes and COVID-19 in the record). Navarixin itself, as MK-7123, caused a dose-dependent decrease in absolute neutrophil count in a COPD trial, with discontinuations at the highest dose. Mouse colitis papers include a selective antagonist that ameliorated acute colitis, but MGI has no single-gene colitis phenotype for it.

Among the JAK kinases the human genetic support sits on JAK2 (Open Targets genetic association [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8458]), with TYK2 lower [gene=TYK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.2863] and JAK1 none [gene=JAK1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.0]; JAK2 and TYK2 carry the interleukin-23 receptor signal, which links this control to IL12B. The JAK inhibitors that worked in UC trials are tofacitinib, a Janus kinase inhibitor that acts more on JAK2- and JAK3-dependent pathways than filgotinib, upadacitinib, a selective JAK1 inhibitor, and filgotinib, a JAK1-preferential inhibitor: the JAK1-selective drugs worked too, so the trials do not show that JAK2 blockade is needed, although JAK1 has no genetic association here, and JAK2 also carries erythropoietin and thrombopoietin receptor signals. Within TYK2, the selective deucravacitinib did not show significant benefit over placebo in UC phase 2, whereas brepocitinib, a TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor, was more effective than placebo in UC phase 2b. The JAK2 result therefore supports the JAK class as a positive control, not a JAK2-selective drug.

cells.text: Neutrophil genes lead the ranking but report cell arrival. In Gubatan 2026 neutrophils make most CXCR2 [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965], CXCL8 [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873] and TREM1 [gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894] transcripts. Smillie 2019 has [type=sc_atlas; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_cell_types=0] neutrophil cell types among its [type=sc_atlas; source=DATASET:SCP259; n_cell_types=51], so it attributes CXCR2 to the few T/NK cells that express it, and that attribution does not replicate in the other atlases. After composition adjustment CXCL8 loses significance (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0525]) and CXCR2 keeps only a small change [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409].

Two increases are changes of the tissue itself. DUOX2 is made by enterocytes [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947] and MMP1 by inflammatory fibroblasts [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]; both attributions replicate in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122, and both keep a clear adjusted change ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161] and [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]). The loss of SLC26A2 is intrinsic [gene=SLC26A2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-1.4638], with almost no neutrophil contribution [gene=SLC26A2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.014].

IDO1, CHI3L1 and CD274 have mixed sources. IDO1 is myeloid in Smillie 2019 but epithelial in Gubatan 2026; CHI3L1 is stromal in Smillie 2019 but myeloid in Gubatan 2026, where neutrophils also contribute [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.466]; CD274 is myeloid-dominant but diffuse, with a large neutrophil share [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]. All three keep a significant change after adjustment ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505], [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967], [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]); the composition model can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so these are partly tissue changes.

spatial.text: In deconvolved Visium spots inflammatory fibroblasts give the largest in-situ contribution to MMP1 [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.568], and the spots with high MMP1 are enriched in inflammatory fibroblasts and neutrophils around them, so tissue and single-cell data agree. CosMx detects MMP1 only at background.
DUOX2 is placed in epithelium by both Xenium and Visium, in agreement with its enterocyte source in the single-cell atlases.

pathways.text: Pathway activity rises broadly in inflamed mucosa. NFkB and TNFa activity are up in all eight cohorts, the NFkB t reaching [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=18.79] in GSE206285, and JAK-STAT, TGFb, EGFR, MAPK, PI3K and Hypoxia are also up in all eight, WNT in seven. STAT3 regulon activity is up in all eight cohorts [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6], as is AP1. Because so many pathways rise together these signals are robust but not specific, and VEGF and Androgen are not consistent across cohorts.

The most specific circuit is neutrophil CXCL8 to CXCR2: in Gubatan 2026 the link from the Neutrophil CXCR4 state to the Neutrophil state rose strongly in inflamed mucosa, a feed-forward recruitment loop, and neutrophil CXCL8 also reaches ACKR1 endothelium. Inflammatory fibroblasts send CXCL1 to CXCR2 on neutrophils at much lower scores, IL1B mainly reaches the decoy receptor IL1R2 on neutrophil states, and the expected neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit is weak. Co-expression is not proof of signalling.

Of the circuit genes, CXCR2 has recorded antagonists, of which reparixin, navarixin, ladarixin and SX-682 are also listed against CXCR1, IL1B has canakinumab, approved outside IBD (cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome in the record), and TREM1 has nangibotide in phase 2; no drug is recorded for CXCL1 or CXCL5.

treatment.text: Gene-level non-response signals are severity markers. Higher baseline CXCR2 (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]), CXCL8 ([gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]), TREM1 ([gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) and IL11 ([gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]) are associated with ustekinumab non-response, but each also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders ([gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126], [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154], [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234], [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]). OSM ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) is not significant in the UNIFI placebo arm ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), yet the drug-by-placebo interaction is not significant either ([gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.974]), so drug specificity is not shown.

At pathway level TNFa is higher in ustekinumab non-responders ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and in several other arms including UNIFI placebo, so it is a severity axis; it is not significant in PURSUIT placebo ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]) or the PROTECT mesalazine arm ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.5-ASA (PROTECT).padj=0.414]). TGFb behaves the same ([type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]; UNIFI placebo [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]). Target expression does not stratify response: IL12B ([gene=IL12B; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.84]) and IL23A ([gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]) for ustekinumab, and ITGB7 for vedolizumab ([gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]). In the adalimumab single-cell atlas CXCL8 shows no baseline difference between remitters and non-remitters.

discovery.text: CHRDL2 has the largest pooled increase of the first-in-class candidates of the discovery screen and is up in [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=7] cohorts. Its transcripts are stromal, mostly inflammatory fibroblasts, and the other single-cell atlases agree [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; other_atlases_agreeing=3]. The increase is partly composition, an antibody is the predicted modality, and no response or functional data exist.

CPXM1 has the second largest increase of the first-in-class candidates. It is stromal in Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122 but epithelial in Gubatan 2026, its increase is partly composition, and genetics and response data are missing.

XKR9 keeps the highest share of its change after composition adjustment among the first-in-class candidates and is one of four epithelial candidates classed intrinsic, but it is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts, the second fewest of the candidates, and lacks response and functional evidence.

integration.text: The streams agree on a core picture. Expression, the paired inflamed and non-inflamed data, the pathway layer and single cells point to a neutrophil-rich inflamed mucosa with NFkB, TNFa and STAT3 activity, with AQP8 showing the largest pooled loss, and the treatment data show that the same neutrophil signals mark severity in drug and placebo arms alike. Genetics and drug history agree for IL12B, and for JAK2 at the level of the JAK class; both have strong Open Targets genetic association with UC ([gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8864] and [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8458]).

They disagree on causality. CXCL8 and CHI3L1, among the largest pooled increases, have no Open Targets genetic association, and CXCL8 is null in plasma Mendelian randomisation, so they read as consequences of inflammation and as biomarkers. For CD274 and CXCL5 genetics runs opposite to an inhibitor, since higher plasma protein lowers risk, and for SLC26A3 the gut eQTL direction is opposite to its loss in biopsies. This atlas has no instrument to test CXCR2 by Mendelian randomisation; one published study found higher CXCR1 and CXCR2 expression with lower UC risk, the direction opposite to an antagonist.

limitations.text: Bulk changes of neutrophil and myeloid genes are confounded by cell influx; the composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so retained fractions are approximate.
Co-expression of ligand and receptor in single cells is not proof of signalling.
The plasma IL12B protein measure (UKB-PPP) does not separate IL-12, IL-23 and free p40, so the Mendelian randomisation result supports the IL-12/IL-23 axis, not anti-p40 over anti-p19 blockade.
Neutrophils also take part in mucosal repair, so blocking their recruitment could slow healing as well as reduce inflammation; CXCR2 antagonists have not gone beyond phase 2 in UC.
Several leading candidates (CXCR2, CXCR1, JAK2) have no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, so their causal direction is untested rather than refuted.

Literature support rests on a few verbatim-checked sentences per gene from a local corpus; the CD274 hub-gene finding of the literature specialist was dropped because its citations are not linked to the gene.
A reading subagent checked every claim against its cited records; claims it found unsupported are listed in the Agents tab rather than removed.

targets.rationale: Positive control for the IL-12/IL-23 axis: a strong Open Targets genetic association with UC [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8864] and the strongest plasma Mendelian randomisation result among this atlas's genes, genetically higher protein raising UC risk [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539] with colocalisation and FinnGen replication, the direction an inhibitor needs. IL12B is the p40 subunit of interleukin-12 and interleukin-23: ustekinumab binds it and worked in UC (UNIFI), and the anti-p19 antibodies mirikizumab, risankizumab and guselkumab, which bind IL23A, worked as well, consistent with the benefit of blocking IL-23. The plasma measure cannot separate the two cytokines (see the limitations).

First in the convergence ranking and up in all eight cohorts, but neutrophils make almost all of its transcripts [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965] and only a small change survives composition adjustment [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]. As a target it was tested and not advanced: two antagonists, SB-656933 and navarixin, went no further than phase 2 in UC, and the antagonist navarixin (as MK-7123) lowered blood neutrophil counts dose-dependently in a COPD trial; a published genetic estimate, from one bioinformatic study, has higher expression going with lower UC risk, the direction opposite to an antagonist. As a biomarker it is higher at baseline in non-responders to ustekinumab and to placebo alike, which marks disease severity rather than response to the drug.

Placed above higher-ranked neutrophil genes because it is a change of the tissue itself: inflammatory fibroblasts make it [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871], Visium places it in the same cells [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.568], it keeps an adjusted change [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636], and it is among the transcripts modified by mirikizumab that track disease activity.

Enterocyte-derived [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], retained after composition adjustment [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161], placed in epithelium by Xenium and Visium and among the most elevated proteins in inflamed biopsies: a tissue biomarker of epithelial antimicrobial stress, with no drug recorded.

Positive control for the JAK class, not a proposal for a JAK2-selective drug. Among the JAK kinases the human genetic support sits on JAK2 [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8458], yet the JAK inhibitors that worked in UC trials are tofacitinib, which acts more on JAK2- and JAK3-dependent pathways than filgotinib, and the selective JAK1 inhibitor upadacitinib and JAK1-preferential filgotinib; the TYK2-selective deucravacitinib did not show significant benefit in UC phase 2, whereas the TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor brepocitinib did. JAK2 also carries erythropoietin and thrombopoietin receptor signals, so selective JAK2 blockade would act on blood cell production. Its expression rises only modestly [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.833].

High in the convergence ranking and up in inflamed mucosa, but genetically higher plasma PD-L1 lowers UC risk [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595], so inhibition runs against genetics; its rise is best read as a compensatory response.

Up in all eight cohorts [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687], but made mostly by neutrophils and myeloid cells, it loses significance after composition adjustment (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0525]), is null in plasma Mendelian randomisation and marks severity in drug and placebo arms alike.

One of the largest pooled RNA increases [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913], retained after adjustment [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967], but the protein change is small [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607] and it has no Open Targets genetic association: a strong tissue biomarker, with targeting only exploratory.

Up in all eight cohorts and replicated as protein [gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917], with a mixed myeloid and epithelial source and an adjusted change [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]; the cited mechanism and inhibitor data come from one study in UC patients and colitis mice, so it is an interferon-response biomarker and at most a repurposing hypothesis.

Made mostly by neutrophils and myeloid cells [gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894], higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa and associated with ustekinumab non-response and placebo non-response alike; nangibotide is recorded in phase 2.

Falls in inflamed mucosa, but higher expression in crypt progenitors raises UC risk [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607], among the strongest colocalising gut eQTL results: the loss in disease may be a response, and the gene is a marker of epithelial transport rather than a target.
Up in all eight cohorts and made mostly by neutrophils, with part of the change retained after adjustment: a tissue marker of neutrophil influx.

Exploratory: the largest pooled increase of the first-in-class candidates, up in [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=7] cohorts, made by stromal cells (mostly inflammatory fibroblasts in Smillie 2019), a lineage all four atlases agree on, and antibody-tractable; partly composition, with no response or functional data.

Exploratory: the highest retained share after composition adjustment among the first-in-class candidates and an epithelial lineage, but up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts and without response or functional evidence.
